name: TitanCart Lite
author: titancart

sections.description:
TitanCart is a complete storefront in one plugin: catalog, cart, checkout, orders, customers, shipping, tax and reporting. It runs on its own database tables and its own REST API rather than bending WordPress posts and meta into a shopping cart, which is why it stays fast as a catalog grows.

No license key is required. TitanCart Lite is free and GPL, and it never contacts a remote server.

What you get

  • Products — simple and variable products, categories, product filters, attributes, image galleries, digital downloads.
  • Cart and checkout — a real cart session, guest checkout, order notes.
  • Payments — Stripe, plus cash on delivery, bank transfer and cheque.
  • Shipping — flat rate, free shipping, and table-based rates with zones and conditions.
  • Tax — full tax classes, zones and rate rules. Not a stripped-down version; tax is a legal requirement, not an upsell.
  • Orders — order management, statuses, invoices, fulfilment and shipment tracking.
  • Customers — accounts, address book, order history, customer groups.
  • Reviews — product reviews with moderation.
  • Wishlists, sitemap, SEO output (meta tags, canonical URLs, Open Graph, JSON-LD product schema), GDPR tools and age verification.
  • Import and export — CSV import and export, including a WooCommerce migration tool.
  • Prism — a free companion storefront theme built for TitanCart, available as a free download from the TitanCart marketplace at market.titancart.io.

Built to be portable

TitanCart’s cart, checkout, order and pricing logic have no WordPress function calls inside them. WordPress is a thin hosting layer over a self-contained engine. That is an architectural choice, not marketing: it is what keeps the query count low and the upgrade path open.

Privacy and external services

TitanCart Lite makes no outbound connections of any kind on its own. It contains no license check, no update checker, no analytics, no telemetry, and no remote code installer. Updates arrive through WordPress.org like any other plugin.

A small number of features contact a third party only after you configure them, using credentials you supply. Each is documented in the External services section below. None is enabled by default.

Source code

The admin interface, admin/build/titancart-admin.js, is hand-written JavaScript and is itself the source code: there is no build step, no transpiler, no JSX, no bundler and no minification anywhere in this plugin. The directory name is historical. The same is true of every other JavaScript and CSS file shipped — what you read in the ZIP is exactly what the developer wrote and maintains.

External services

TitanCart Lite connects to the following external services. Every connection is off by default and happens only after the site owner configures the feature with their own credentials or explicitly triggers it with a click.

Stripe (payment processing)

  • What it is: card payment processing by Stripe, Inc.
  • What it is used for: charging customers at checkout when the store owner has created a Stripe payment method with their own API keys.
  • What data is sent, and when: when a Stripe method is enabled, the checkout page loads Stripe’s Stripe.js from js.stripe.com (a Stripe requirement for PCI compliance) and card details entered by the customer go directly from the customer’s browser to Stripe — they never touch the store’s server. The server then exchanges payment intents/confirmations with Stripe’s API (order amount, currency, and the payment reference).
  • Terms and privacy: Stripe Services Agreement, Stripe Privacy Policy.

Google reCAPTCHA (spam and abuse protection)

  • What it is: Google’s reCAPTCHA v2/v3 service.
  • What it is used for: protecting the login, registration, checkout, review and contact surfaces from bots — only if the store owner enables the reCAPTCHA feature and supplies their own site key and secret.
  • What data is sent, and when: on pages with a protected form, Google’s api.js loads from www.google.com in the visitor’s browser (Google’s script collects the signals it uses for its bot score — see its privacy policy); on submit, the server sends the response token, the site secret and the visitor’s IP address to Google’s siteverify endpoint to obtain the verdict.
  • Terms and privacy: Google Terms of Service, Google Privacy Policy.

Cloudflare Turnstile (spam and abuse protection — alternative to reCAPTCHA)

  • What it is: Cloudflare’s Turnstile bot-detection service.
  • What it is used for: protecting the same login, registration, checkout, review and contact surfaces from bots — only if the store owner selects Turnstile as the bot-protection provider and supplies their own Turnstile site key and secret key.
  • What data is sent, and when: on pages with a protected form, Cloudflare’s api.js loads from challenges.cloudflare.com in the visitor’s browser (the script collects the signals Cloudflare uses for its verdict — see its privacy policy); on submit, the server sends the response token, the secret key and the visitor’s IP address to Cloudflare’s siteverify endpoint to obtain the verdict.
  • Terms and privacy: Cloudflare Website and Online Services Terms of Use, Cloudflare Privacy Policy.

Google Maps Places (address autocomplete)

  • What it is: the Google Maps JavaScript API with the Places library.
  • What it is used for: suggesting street addresses as a customer types on the checkout and account address forms — only if the store owner turns on Address autocomplete in checkout settings and supplies their own Google Maps API key. Off by default; nothing loads without the key.
  • What data is sent, and when: on the checkout and account pages only, the visitor’s browser loads maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/js (keyed with the owner’s API key) and sends the characters typed into the address field to Google to receive suggestions. The store’s server never contacts Google for this feature.
  • Terms and privacy: Google Maps Platform Terms, Google Privacy Policy.

YouTube and Vimeo (product video embeds)

  • What it is: the public video players of YouTube (Google) and Vimeo.
  • What it is used for: showing a product video on the product page when the store owner has pasted a YouTube or Vimeo link into that product’s video field. No video is embedded unless the owner adds one.
  • What data is sent, and when: the product page renders a thumbnail from img.youtube.com and, when the visitor clicks play, an embedded player from www.youtube.com or player.vimeo.com in the visitor’s browser; those providers receive the visitor’s request as with any embedded video. In the admin product editor, a thumbnail preview is fetched from img.youtube.com for the link the owner entered. Videos hosted on the store’s own server are played directly and involve no third party.
  • Terms and privacy: YouTube Terms of Service, Google Privacy Policy, Vimeo Terms of Service, Vimeo Privacy Policy.

Remote images during CSV import

  • What it is: standard HTTP downloads performed by WordPress itself.
  • What it is used for: when the store owner runs a product CSV import whose rows contain image URLs, WordPress downloads those images into the media library.
  • What data is sent, and when: an HTTP GET to each image URL the owner provided in their own file, at import time only.

Demo content for the Prism theme (market.titancart.io)

  • What it is: ready-made demo packages (products, categories, attributes and banner images) published by TitanCart for its free Prism storefront theme, which is a separate download.
  • What it is used for: letting a store owner who has installed Prism fill an empty store with matching sample content from Theme Options → Demo content → Install demo, and later reinstall, clear or remove it.
  • What data is sent, and when: only when the owner clicks Install, Switch or Reinstall does the server fetch the list of available demos and then the chosen package (a JSON file plus its images) from market.titancart.io over HTTPS — ordinary GET requests carrying no store data. Opening the Theme Options page does not contact the service. Nothing is fetched on sites without Prism.
  • Terms and privacy: TitanCart Privacy Policy.

The product page’s optional share buttons are ordinary links to Facebook, X, Pinterest and LinkedIn share pages; nothing is loaded from those sites and no request is made unless the visitor clicks one.

No other external connections exist in TitanCart Lite. Payment gateways beyond Stripe (PayPal, Square, Authorize.net), live carrier shipping rates (USPS, FedEx), social sign-in (Google, Facebook, Apple) and the TitanCart extensions catalog are features of TitanCart Pro, are not present in this plugin’s code, and are documented in the Pro edition’s own materials.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins → Add New and search for “TitanCart”.
  2. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  3. Open TitanCart → Settings to set your store details, currency, payment, shipping and tax. There is no setup wizard; the store setup checklist at https://help.titancart.io/docs/store-setup-checklist/ walks through the order.
  4. Optionally install the free Prism storefront theme, available from the TitanCart marketplace at market.titancart.io.

No account, key or sign-up is required.
sections.faq:
Do I need a license key?

No. TitanCart Lite is free, GPL-licensed, and fully functional without a key. It never asks for one and never phones home.

Will it work alongside WooCommerce?

TitanCart does not use, extend or depend on WooCommerce, and it stores nothing in WooCommerce’s tables. Running both at once is not recommended simply because two storefronts on one site confuses customers, not because they conflict technically. There is a built-in WooCommerce importer to migrate your catalog across.

Does it slow my site down?

TitanCart uses its own indexed tables instead of wp_postmeta, so catalog queries do not scale with your meta table. The admin is a single-page app that loads once and then talks to a REST API.

What is the difference between Lite and Pro?

Lite is a complete, working store: products, cart, checkout, Stripe, shipping, tax, orders, customers, reviews, import/export and SEO. Pro adds promotions, coupon codes and discount rules, loyalty rewards, gift cards, product bundles and options, email campaigns, returns (RMA), advanced reporting, additional payment gateways, live carrier shipping rates, the external REST API, and the first-party extension suite.

Everything in Lite stays in Lite. Pro is additional capability, never a paywall in front of something that used to be free.

Where is my data stored?

In your own database, in tables prefixed wp_tc_. Nothing is stored off-site. Uninstalling is a clean removal.
sections.changelog:
0.2.78

  • New: Cloudflare Turnstile can replace Google reCAPTCHA. Extensions → Bot Protection (reCAPTCHA / Turnstile) → Provider; paste the Turnstile site key and secret key from your Cloudflare dashboard (the widget’s Managed / Non-interactive / Invisible mode is chosen there). Existing reCAPTCHA keys and settings are untouched; the default stays reCAPTCHA v2. Visitors now see “Please complete the verification.” and “Verification failed. Please try again.” whichever provider is on.
  • Fixed: CSV exports (Import / Export, the Categories exports, Revenue Reports) are no longer written as public files under wp-content/uploads — anyone holding the link could read customer and order data for 24 hours without logging in. The Download link is now an admin-only address that builds the file when opened and expires after 15 minutes; nothing is stored on disk. Files from earlier versions are still removed by the hourly clean-up.
  • New: the Company a customer enters at registration is now on their record — shown in the customer editor and under My Account → Profile, included in the customers export and pre-filled at checkout. Before, it was stored where nothing read it.
  • Fixed: Appearance → “Product list default sorting” applies to the first page of the shop, category, tag and brand pages and of [titancart_shop]. The first page was always newest-first while the sort box and the following pages used the setting, so page 2 skipped or repeated products.
  • Fixed: Appearance → “Products per page” is limited to 48, the most the storefront loads per page; a larger value showed N products on page 1 and 48 on every later page, and 0 broke the category, tag and brand pages.
  • Fixed: shop paging — the address bar now follows the page buttons, so page 2 can be bookmarked, shared and returned to with Back; Load more and infinite scroll continue from the page that was opened (they restarted at page 2); each page is its own canonical address, on a [titancart_shop] page too. The [titancart_shop] status attribute, which never reached the following pages, is removed — the shortcode lists active products.
  • Fixed: a published page that still contains [titancart_gift_cards] on an edition without the Gift Cards feature printed the shortcode as text.
  • Fixed: Storefront → Pages — assigning FAQ, Testimonials or Gift Cards to a page that does not contain the feature’s shortcode now shows a warning under the selector (the page is still saved; pages built with Elementor are recognised).
  • Fixed: product editor — a chosen category now shows its parent path (“Accessories · Electronics”) so two categories with the same name can be told apart; the category picker loads up to 500 categories (was 200).
  • Fixed: customer editor — the address card is titled Billing Address or Shipping Address after the address it shows; an imported customer’s billing address was labelled “Shipping Address”.
  • Fixed: CSV import — a file with Product Code and URL Slug only no longer fails the pre-run check with “Product name is required”; a name is required only for a product that does not exist yet. A name made only of symbols now gets its slug from the Product Code. The categories Status hint lists H = Hidden.
  • Fixed: CSV import — a row the pre-run check flagged was still written when you continued past the errors (a row without a name became a blank, published product). The same check now runs row by row during the import: a flagged row is skipped and logged as “Row N: reason”, or fails the import when skipping errors is off. The upload step now shows the server’s reason instead of a bare “Upload failed.”.
  • Fixed: CSV import (orders) — the pre-run check no longer flags the Status of a row that updates an existing order, where the status is never written.
  • Changed: products export — the Quantity, Track Inventory and Images columns now use the importer’s labels (were Stock Qty, Inventory Tracking, Image URLs), so a re-import maps them automatically.
  • Fixed: an upload that was never started no longer sits in Recent Imports as “queued” and then “failed — timed out”; it is removed with its file after 24 hours. A job that times out now loses its uploaded file too.
  • Fixed: cancelling an import in its final seconds could leave it marked “Import Complete” without the “Cancelled by…” line in its log.
  • Database: Migration 86 — adds the Company column to customers and copies the values saved by earlier registrations.

0.2.77

  • Fixed: CSV import — an empty Description, Short Description, Meta Title or Meta Description cell erased the saved text of a product that already existed (a price-list update with an empty Description column wiped every description). An empty cell now changes nothing anywhere in a products, categories or customers import.
  • Fixed: CSV import — a product’s URL slug was regenerated from its name on every re-import, replacing a hand-set address; it is now written only when the file supplies one or the product has none. A file with just Product Code and URL Slug now updates the slug, supplied and auto-created product and category slugs are made unique, and a deleted product’s slug no longer forces “-2” on a live one.
  • Fixed: CSV import — the first entry of the Categories column is now the product’s one main category. A re-import with a different first entry used to leave the product with two main categories.
  • Fixed: CSV import (customers) — empty Company, Address 2, City, State, Postcode or Country cells no longer blank the customer’s saved billing address.
  • New: CSV import — the check before a run now covers orders, order items, product reviews and waitlist files (e-mail, order status, rating, known order number and Product Code), and List Price / Cost Price must be numeric.
  • Fixed: the Import / Export clean-up never ran. Exported CSV files are now deleted after 24 hours, as the page has always said, and an import with no progress for 24 hours is marked failed. After updating, export files older than a day are removed at the first hourly run.
  • Fixed: import wizard — cancelling a job from Recent Imports now ends the wizard with “Import Cancelled” instead of leaving “Processing in background…”; Recent Imports refreshes when a job ends, says why a Cancel was refused, and each job has a Log you can open.
  • Changed: products export — Categories now holds the main category as a full Parent///Child path, and a new Secondary Categories column holds the rest. This is the format the importer reads, so an export re-imports into the same tree. Note: re-importing a products export made before this version sets each product’s main category to the first name in its Categories cell.
  • Fixed: a WordPress page carrying [titancart_shop] — sorting, filters, the view toggle and the page buttons did nothing. They work now, the page buttons are real links, and per_page is limited to 48.
  • Fixed: the product page printed “Free shipping & returns: On all orders over $200!” and “Estimated Delivery: 5–10 business days” on every store. Both lines are gone; an extension can still print a delivery estimate there.
  • Fixed: an unknown product-tag address now answers 404 instead of an empty tag page, and a tag with a non-Latin name (Cyrillic, Greek, CJK…) now shows its products instead of an empty page.
  • Fixed: product reviews import — a Status written with a capital (“Pending”) was stored as approved.
  • Fixed: [titancart_wishlist], [titancart_reviews] and [titancart_review_form] were printed as raw text when the feature was switched off.
  • Fixed: adding a customer through the REST API without a password is refused instead of creating a record nobody can sign in to.
  • Database: Migration 85 — clears duplicate main-category links left by earlier imports and schedules the Import / Export clean-up.

0.2.76

  • Fixed: Customers → + Add Customer with a password saved the login but not the record — the Status, phone, date of birth, notes and address typed on the form were lost, no welcome e-mail went out, and the form stayed open (“A customer with this email already exists.” on a second Save). The record is now saved in full and opens after Save.
  • Fixed: on a store installed fresh, the Wholesale customer group was offered on the registration form (sign-up mode Open); new installs now start with Customer = Open, Wholesale = Apply, Guest = Closed, as updated stores already do.
  • Fixed: a customer who deleted their own account under My Account kept their customer-group memberships, and those invisible rows could stop you deleting the group (“still used by N members” with an empty Members page). The self-delete now removes them and the check counts only live customers.
  • Fixed: a guest who later registered with the same e-mail lost the phone number from their order when the registration form had no phone box.
  • Database: Migration 84 — removes customer-group membership rows whose customer no longer exists or was deleted.

0.2.75

  • New: Customers → Customer Groups — membership is administered at last. Each group has a Members list (add a customer by name or e-mail, set a row to Active / Pending / Declined, remove), the customer’s own page has a Customer Groups card, and a Requests tab lists pending applications with Approve / Decline.
  • New: customer groups you apply for. Each group now has a sign-up mode — Open (offered on the registration form), Apply (the customer applies under My Account → Customer Groups and you approve or decline, with an e-mail either way) or Closed (members are added by you). Every registered customer is in the Customer group automatically, including existing ones; the Wholesale group becomes apply-for on upgrade; the Marketplace’s Vendors group stays managed by the Marketplace.
  • Fixed: a shopper could pick Wholesale (or, on a marketplace store, Vendors) on the registration form and join at once.
  • Fixed: a customer who signed up with Google, Facebook or Apple skipped “Administrator must activate new accounts” and got no welcome e-mail, admin notice, sign-up bonus or webhook; they are now registered the same way as a form sign-up.
  • Fixed: an unknown product, category or brand address answered 200 to a HEAD request (crawlers and link checkers) while the page said “not found”; a product set to Hidden is reachable by direct link, like a hidden category.
  • Fixed: Settings → Import / Export — a queued or running import can be cancelled, and an import left with no progress for 24 hours is marked failed instead of sitting forever.
  • Fixed: Settings → API & Integrations — a burst of parallel calls on one key could pass the rate limit; the counter is atomic now.
  • Fixed: Settings → Security → Minimum password length below 6 was accepted but never applied; it is floored at 6, the storefront forms show the configured length, and passwords set in the admin are checked too. The Currencies page note names the primary-currency rule instead of a setting that did not exist.
  • Fixed: My Account “Total Spent” now excludes refunded orders (the same rule Revenue Reports uses); a WordPress sign-in error no longer shows “” literally.
  • Database: Migration 83 — sign-up modes on the seeded groups, the Customer-group back-fill, an atomic API rate counter, a cancelled import status, and the three customer-group e-mail templates revived under Settings → Notifications.

0.2.74

  • Changed: a customer whose account is Disabled (awaiting approval, or deactivated) or Banned can no longer sign in anywhere — wp-login.php, the My Account form, the shortcode form, Google / Facebook / Apple sign-in and Application Passwords — and their open sessions end when the status is changed. Previously only the My Account form checked, and only for Disabled. Administrators are exempt.
  • Fixed: Customers → Customer Groups — deleting a group left its members, Bulk Buys price tiers, Loyalty Rewards rates and subscription-plan links pointing at a group that no longer existed (and they kept paying out). Delete is now refused while anything uses the group, with the counts shown; the built-in Guest, Customer, Wholesale and Vendors groups cannot be deleted; renaming a group no longer changes its internal handle; a duplicate name is reported instead of silently creating nothing; the page shows each group’s member count and every server error.
  • Changed: a Disabled customer group no longer grants its members tier pricing, catalog promotions or loyalty rates — the advertised behaviour.
  • Fixed: Customers → Customers — the Search card’s Name, Phone and E-mail boxes work as three filters (Phone never matched before); changing a customer’s e-mail now changes their WordPress login e-mail too; notes keep their line breaks; a new default address replaces the previous default instead of sitting beside it; deleting a customer schedules the anonymisation of their orders that the card already promised and clears their group memberships; the Spent column uses the store currency; the Tax exempt and Language fields (never saved / one option) are gone until built; the Administrators Status radio (never sent) is gone — change the role instead; Last login is now recorded.
  • Fixed: My Account dashboard “Total Orders / Total Spent” counted only the most recent page of orders. The GDPR export’s wishlist section was always empty. The Delete-account button on the profile page read the wrong setting. Password minimum aligned to 6 everywhere.
  • Fixed: Settings → Customer Fields — the Show / Required boxes on built-in rows (name, e-mail, address…) did nothing; they are no longer offered and the hint says what the page does. Field labels can be edited. Five field types that rendered as a plain text box are no longer offered for new fields. The seeded second address line is labelled “Address line 2”.
  • Fixed: Settings — “Minimum search query length” was saved in one place and read from another (inert); 15 Logging toggles that no code ever wrote to are gone, and “Shipping rate errors” / “Settings changes” now govern the rows they name; “Products per page” shows the value the storefront uses (24); the packing slip uses TitanCart’s date format like the invoice; the Social Login and Site Backup cards describe what exists; the Currencies page says that extra currencies are stored for reference only.
  • Fixed: storefront shortcodes — [titancart_account] showed the login panel to signed-in customers; [titancart_cart], [titancart_checkout] and [titancart_account] on a page rendered the theme header twice and without TitanCart’s styles and scripts; [titancart_shop] pagination was stuck on page 1. The fallback header no longer advertises “Free shipping on orders over $50” or links FAQ / Contact / About / Careers to pages that may not exist. An unknown category address returns 404 instead of the shop index; an unknown My Account section says so; a notice asks for pretty permalinks when WordPress is on Plain.
  • Fixed: Settings → API & Integrations — every keyed Store API call counted twice against the key’s rate limit and was logged twice (WordPress runs a route’s permission check again to build the Allow header). Once now.
  • Changed: Settings → Import / Export history reads “N of M rows processed”.
  • Database: two additive columns for customer groups you apply for (coming): membership status and per-group sign-up mode. Existing data is unaffected.

0.2.73

  • Fixed: none of the Import Settings (import strategy, test import, skip rows with errors, delete additional images, set quantity to zero) reached the import — they were posted as one field the server did not decode — so every import stopped at its first bad row and “Update existing” never applied. They are honoured now.
  • Fixed: Settings → Import / Export processed every row after a failed row a second time (duplicate reviews, order items and addresses) and a file whose last rows kept failing re-ran every 5 seconds forever. Progress now counts rows read separately from rows imported, and a job always finishes.
  • Fixed: “Perform test import — only the first 5 rows” imported up to 100 rows. It stops at 5.
  • Fixed: an order imported with a status the store does not have was saved with no status and hidden from every list. Unknown statuses are now reported as row errors; the single letters the old hint suggested (P, C, O…) are translated to the matching status, and the sample orders file uses status names.
  • Fixed: a blank cell in a yes/no column (Featured, Track Inventory, Free Shipping…) switched the setting off on update, and “no” switched it on. Blank cells are now left alone and no / false / off mean no.
  • Fixed: a categories import set to “Create new only” created the same categories again on every run, and blank cells wiped existing descriptions. Customers are matched to an existing record (including a guest who ordered before) instead of adding a second one, and a re-import updates the customer’s billing address instead of adding another. Imported customers no longer carry an unregistered role.
  • Fixed: the import’s Tax Class, Search Words, Out-of-stock Action and category Position columns were accepted but never saved; they are saved now. “Page Title” is no longer offered (there is no such field).
  • Fixed: a required field left unmapped no longer starts an import that fails on every row, and a column headed “ID” is no longer auto-mapped to Width. Image download failures are written to the job log and System Logs.
  • Fixed: Storefront → SEO — “Canonical URLs” and “Noindex filter pages” were saved but never read, and the robots.txt tab was never served. Both toggles work, the robots.txt text is served (with the sitemap line), the Default Meta Templates are applied to products without their own title or description, and the cart, checkout, account and search pages are marked noindex. The “Trailing slash” toggle is gone: WordPress Settings → Permalinks already decides it.
  • Fixed: with Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress or All in One SEO active, TitanCart no longer adds a second canonical tag, document title or Product structured data.
  • Fixed: a sub-category answered at two addresses with a self-referencing canonical on each; the nested address now redirects to the one the catalog links to. Image alt text left blank falls back to the product name. SEO queries follow the storefront language instead of always English.
  • Fixed (Pro): Sales → Revenue Reports — the Tax tab was empty on every store; the per-rate tax lines are now recorded with each new order (orders placed earlier appear as one combined line). Export CSV exports the period shown, not just today; the Referrals tab’s Export works; Net Revenue no longer subtracts coupon discounts twice; the Products tab shows one row per product with a quantity-weighted average price; New Customers counts customer records, not WordPress users; the Sales tab has a pager; export files are cleaned up hourly as advertised.
  • Fixed (Pro): the Store API behind Settings → API & Integrations keys never answered with a key — its routes were taken by the public catalog routes. Keyed routes now live under /api/store/, call the real catalog, log every request to the key’s Logs panel, return 403 for a revoked key, send a Retry-After header when rate-limited, and a webhook’s generated signing secret is shown once on creation.
  • Fixed: a shopper signing in with Google, Facebook or Apple for the first time on an existing WordPress account now gets a customer record straight away, not on the next My Account visit.

0.2.71

  • Fixed: the “Save your details for next time” card shown after a guest checkout failed with “reCAPTCHA verification failed” on stores where reCAPTCHA protects registration, because the card did not show the reCAPTCHA check. The card now carries it, so the account is created in place.

0.2.70

  • Fixed: a shopper who had checked out as a guest and later created an account with the same e-mail address (including from the “Save your details for next time” card after checkout) got an account TitanCart could not load: My Account greeted “Hello, there!” with no orders, and Customers kept a second, unlinked record. The guest record is now attached to the new account, so earlier guest orders, addresses and totals appear under it. The same applies when such a shopper signs in for the first time or an administrator creates the account from Customers → Add Customer.
  • Fixed: the account page built from the [titancart_account] shortcode stopped with a PHP error when General Settings → Customers → “Allow customer to sign up for customer group” was on (the template called a database method that does not exist and read a column that does not exist). The Customer Group dropdown now lists the same groups as the My Account page: active groups except Guest and groups granted by a subscription plan.
  • Fixed: on that shortcode page the Customer Group dropdown was hidden until the setting had been saved once; it now follows the setting’s default (on).

0.2.69

  • Fixed: orders paid by Check, Bank Transfer or Cash on Delivery could not be refunded from the order page (“No completed payment found for this order”). The payment is now recorded as received when the order enters Processing or Completed, and existing paid offline orders are updated on upgrade.
  • Fixed: a refund of part of an offline-paid order no longer moves the order to Refunded; only a refund of the full total does, as with card payments.
  • Fixed: Settings → Order Statuses let a status be deleted while orders still used it (the check read a column that does not exist). The seven built-in order statuses and the default fulfillment status can be renamed and recoloured but no longer deleted; a status in use by orders or shipments is refused with the count.
  • Fixed: the Position typed when creating a status was ignored; the Gift Card Statuses tab, which nothing read, is gone; the retired “Reduce” inventory action is no longer accepted.
  • Fixed: the order-received page after checkout showed built-in status names and colours of its own and the raw handle for a custom status; it now shows the name and colour set under Settings → Order Statuses.
  • Fixed: Extensions → Updates showed a permanent “Up to date” and a fictitious update-history entry; the indicator now reflects the last check, the history card is gone, TitanCart itself is updated from WordPress → Plugins, and core no longer lists itself under Purchased Extensions.
  • Fixed: on Sales → Fulfillment the shipment note was labelled as internal although it is e-mailed to the customer; it is now “Note to the customer”. The Shipping Method shown on a shipment falls back to the order’s method, the Create Shipment search covers every status the Needs Fulfillment queue uses, and digital items are no longer offered for shipping.
  • Fixed: the Issue Refund window showed “$” and “USD” for every store; it now uses the order’s currency, and Square refunds are requested in the order’s currency.
  • Fixed: the System Logs toggles “Refunds” and “Refund processed” never produced a row; every refund is now logged under both.
  • Changed: the Cancelled e-mail no longer promises a refund within 5–10 business days (cancelling an order does not move money); stores that never edited that template receive the new wording on upgrade.

0.2.68

  • Fixed: Sales → Active Carts → opening a cart showed “Cart Items (0)” and a $0 subtotal for every cart; the detail page now lists the cart’s items with their product codes.
  • Fixed: guest rows on Sales → Active Carts had no label; they now read “Session” followed by the session’s short id.

0.2.67

  • Fixed: every TitanCart page (shop, product, cart, checkout, account, search) told WordPress it was the blog index — the page carried the “blog” body class, and on a store whose homepage shows the latest posts, themes showed the blog header and SEO plugins printed the homepage title on every product page. TitanCart pages are now plain pages to WordPress.
  • Fixed: the “View all results” link in the search suggestions dropdown pointed at the site root; it now uses the store’s search page, so it works when WordPress is installed in a sub-folder.
  • Fixed: product, attribute and order-item names read by the order confirmation page, the printable invoice, the CSV import / export and the API always used English; they now follow the store’s language (WPML, Polylang or the WordPress site language, limited to the languages set up under Settings → Languages).

0.2.66

  • Added: back-in-stock e-mails go out by themselves. When a product that shoppers signed up for comes back into stock — through the product editor, Bulk Edit, a CSV import, a returned order or an order edit — the people on its Waitlist tab receive the “Back in Stock Notification” e-mail, oldest sign-ups first. Two new settings under Settings → General Settings → Catalog: “Notify the waitlist automatically” (on) and “Back-in-stock e-mails per restock” (match the quantity restocked, at least 10). Notify All on the Waitlist tab still e-mails everyone waiting.
  • Changed: the low-stock alert now fires from every way stock can change — typing a new quantity in the product editor, Bulk Edit, a CSV import and the WooCommerce import — not only from sales and order edits. When several products fall into the low-stock band in one update you receive one “Low Stock Digest” e-mail listing them instead of one e-mail per product (new template under Settings → Notifications → Templates).
  • Fixed: since 0.2.65 the “Back in Stock Notification” e-mail greeted the shopper with the raw placeholder {customer_first_name}; the name is filled in again (“there” when the sign-up had no name).

0.2.65

  • Added: a shipment e-mail. Tick “E-mail the customer about this shipment” when you create a shipment under Sales → Fulfillment and the customer receives the “Order Shipped” e-mail with the items in that shipment, the carrier, the tracking number and a Track button. Changing the tracking number of an existing shipment with the box ticked sends “Tracking information updated”. Both are templates under Settings → Notifications → Templates.
  • Changed: every remaining e-mail now renders its template under Settings → Notifications → Templates — the gift card, the return e-mails (requested, approved, declined, completed), the account e-mails, the back-in-stock, low-stock and new-review notices. No row is marked “Built-in layout” any more; editing the subject or body changes what is sent. Templates you edited keep your edits; untouched ones move to the branded layout with your logo, colour and company footer.
  • Added: the Department E-mail Addresses under Settings → General Settings → Company now work. The user department is the From address of the account e-mails; the support department becomes the Reply-To of every customer e-mail and is available as the {support_email} placeholder; the newsletter Reply-To is set on every campaign.
  • Added: “Account details were updated” (Settings → Notifications, Account group) — sent when a customer changes their own details under My Account. Off until you switch it on.
  • Added: “Live shipping rates failed” (System group) — when USPS, UPS or FedEx rejects a live-rate request, the store administrator gets at most one e-mail per carrier per hour and every failure is listed under Settings → System Logs. Off until you switch it on.
  • Changed: the e-mail to the administrator about an order status change has its own subject, so it is no longer threaded under the customer’s e-mail in Gmail.
  • Fixed: the “New return request” e-mail went to the order department; it now goes to the site administrator address like every other administrator notice.

0.2.64

  • Changed: every order e-mail (confirmation, new-order notice to the administrator, order received while a card payment is authorised or under review, status changes to the customer and the administrator, download links) is now sent from its template under Settings → Notifications → Templates. Editing the subject or body there changes what is sent; before, the edits were saved but the mails used a fixed layout.
  • Changed: the status e-mail templates are now named after your order statuses (Pending, Processing, On Hold, Completed, Cancelled, Refunded, Failed) with a generic “other statuses” template for statuses you add. Existing templates keep any edits you made.
  • Added: template placeholders for the items table, totals, addresses, payment instructions, download links, invoice link, payment and shipping method, tracking number, and more; the Templates tab lists them.
  • Fixed: the “View your order” button in order e-mails pointed at a page that does not exist. It now opens the order under My Account → Orders.
  • Fixed: saving a template no longer drops the document type line at the top of the body.
  • Changed: the Test Email tab and the template editor’s “Send test” now send the same template the store sends, with sample order data.

0.2.63

  • Fixed: a review posted by a shopper who was not signed in failed with a server error after it had been saved: the review reached the Pending list but the shopper saw an error instead of the confirmation, and the “New product review” e-mail to the store administrator was not sent. Affected 0.2.60 through 0.2.62.

0.2.62

  • Fixed: after posting a review on a store that moderates reviews, coming back to the product page said “You have already submitted a review for this product.” as if the review had been refused. The page now says the review is awaiting approval while it is pending and “You have already reviewed this product.” once it is published, and the message shown right after submitting says the same.
  • Changed: with “Only buyers can review” on, a signed-in customer who has no completed …

short_description: A self-hosted eCommerce engine for WordPress. Own tables, own REST API, own admin. No extra plugins. No page-builder bloat.
description:
TitanCart is a complete storefront in one plugin: catalog, cart, checkout, orders, customers, shipping, tax and reporting. It runs on its own database tables and its own REST API rather than bending WordPress posts and meta into a shopping cart, which is why it stays fast as a catalog grows.

No license key is required. TitanCart Lite is free and GPL, and it never contacts a remote server.

What you get

  • Products — simple and variable products, categories, product filters, attributes, image galleries, digital downloads.
  • Cart and checkout — a real cart session, guest checkout, order notes.
  • Payments — Stripe, plus cash on delivery, bank transfer and cheque.
  • Shipping — flat rate, free shipping, and table-based rates with zones and conditions.
  • Tax — full tax classes, zones and rate rules. Not a stripped-down version; tax is a legal requirement, not an upsell.
  • Orders — order management, statuses, invoices, fulfilment and shipment tracking.
  • Customers — accounts, address book, order history, customer groups.
  • Reviews — product reviews with moderation.
  • Wishlists, sitemap, SEO output (meta tags, canonical URLs, Open Graph, JSON-LD product schema), GDPR tools and age verification.
  • Import and export — CSV import and export, including a WooCommerce migration tool.
  • Prism — a free companion storefront theme built for TitanCart, available as a free download from the TitanCart marketplace at market.titancart.io.

Built to be portable

TitanCart’s cart, checkout, order and pricing logic have no WordPress function calls inside them. WordPress is a thin hosting layer over a self-contained engine. That is an architectural choice, not marketing: it is what keeps the query count low and the upgrade path open.

Privacy and external services

TitanCart Lite makes no outbound connections of any kind on its own. It contains no license check, no update checker, no analytics, no telemetry, and no remote code installer. Updates arrive through WordPress.org like any other plugin.

A small number of features contact a third party only after you configure them, using credentials you supply. Each is documented in the External services section below. None is enabled by default.

Source code

The admin interface, admin/build/titancart-admin.js, is hand-written JavaScript and is itself the source code: there is no build step, no transpiler, no JSX, no bundler and no minification anywhere in this plugin. The directory name is historical. The same is true of every other JavaScript and CSS file shipped — what you read in the ZIP is exactly what the developer wrote and maintains.

External services

TitanCart Lite connects to the following external services. Every connection is off by default and happens only after the site owner configures the feature with their own credentials or explicitly triggers it with a click.

Stripe (payment processing)

  • What it is: card payment processing by Stripe, Inc.
  • What it is used for: charging customers at checkout when the store owner has created a Stripe payment method with their own API keys.
  • What data is sent, and when: when a Stripe method is enabled, the checkout page loads Stripe’s Stripe.js from js.stripe.com (a Stripe requirement for PCI compliance) and card details entered by the customer go directly from the customer’s browser to Stripe — they never touch the store’s server. The server then exchanges payment intents/confirmations with Stripe’s API (order amount, currency, and the payment reference).
  • Terms and privacy: Stripe Services Agreement, Stripe Privacy Policy.

Google reCAPTCHA (spam and abuse protection)

  • What it is: Google’s reCAPTCHA v2/v3 service.
  • What it is used for: protecting the login, registration, checkout, review and contact surfaces from bots — only if the store owner enables the reCAPTCHA feature and supplies their own site key and secret.
  • What data is sent, and when: on pages with a protected form, Google’s api.js loads from www.google.com in the visitor’s browser (Google’s script collects the signals it uses for its bot score — see its privacy policy); on submit, the server sends the response token, the site secret and the visitor’s IP address to Google’s siteverify endpoint to obtain the verdict.
  • Terms and privacy: Google Terms of Service, Google Privacy Policy.

Cloudflare Turnstile (spam and abuse protection — alternative to reCAPTCHA)

  • What it is: Cloudflare’s Turnstile bot-detection service.
  • What it is used for: protecting the same login, registration, checkout, review and contact surfaces from bots — only if the store owner selects Turnstile as the bot-protection provider and supplies their own Turnstile site key and secret key.
  • What data is sent, and when: on pages with a protected form, Cloudflare’s api.js loads from challenges.cloudflare.com in the visitor’s browser (the script collects the signals Cloudflare uses for its verdict — see its privacy policy); on submit, the server sends the response token, the secret key and the visitor’s IP address to Cloudflare’s siteverify endpoint to obtain the verdict.
  • Terms and privacy: Cloudflare Website and Online Services Terms of Use, Cloudflare Privacy Policy.

Google Maps Places (address autocomplete)

  • What it is: the Google Maps JavaScript API with the Places library.
  • What it is used for: suggesting street addresses as a customer types on the checkout and account address forms — only if the store owner turns on Address autocomplete in checkout settings and supplies their own Google Maps API key. Off by default; nothing loads without the key.
  • What data is sent, and when: on the checkout and account pages only, the visitor’s browser loads maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/js (keyed with the owner’s API key) and sends the characters typed into the address field to Google to receive suggestions. The store’s server never contacts Google for this feature.
  • Terms and privacy: Google Maps Platform Terms, Google Privacy Policy.

YouTube and Vimeo (product video embeds)

  • What it is: the public video players of YouTube (Google) and Vimeo.
  • What it is used for: showing a product video on the product page when the store owner has pasted a YouTube or Vimeo link into that product’s video field. No video is embedded unless the owner adds one.
  • What data is sent, and when: the product page renders a thumbnail from img.youtube.com and, when the visitor clicks play, an embedded player from www.youtube.com or player.vimeo.com in the visitor’s browser; those providers receive the visitor’s request as with any embedded video. In the admin product editor, a thumbnail preview is fetched from img.youtube.com for the link the owner entered. Videos hosted on the store’s own server are played directly and involve no third party.
  • Terms and privacy: YouTube Terms of Service, Google Privacy Policy, Vimeo Terms of Service, Vimeo Privacy Policy.

Remote images during CSV import

  • What it is: standard HTTP downloads performed by WordPress itself.
  • What it is used for: when the store owner runs a product CSV import whose rows contain image URLs, WordPress downloads those images into the media library.
  • What data is sent, and when: an HTTP GET to each image URL the owner provided in their own file, at import time only.

Demo content for the Prism theme (market.titancart.io)

  • What it is: ready-made demo packages (products, categories, attributes and banner images) published by TitanCart for its free Prism storefront theme, which is a separate download.
  • What it is used for: letting a store owner who has installed Prism fill an empty store with matching sample content from Theme Options → Demo content → Install demo, and later reinstall, clear or remove it.
  • What data is sent, and when: only when the owner clicks Install, Switch or Reinstall does the server fetch the list of available demos and then the chosen package (a JSON file plus its images) from market.titancart.io over HTTPS — ordinary GET requests carrying no store data. Opening the Theme Options page does not contact the service. Nothing is fetched on sites without Prism.
  • Terms and privacy: TitanCart Privacy Policy.

The product page’s optional share buttons are ordinary links to Facebook, X, Pinterest and LinkedIn share pages; nothing is loaded from those sites and no request is made unless the visitor clicks one.

No other external connections exist in TitanCart Lite. Payment gateways beyond Stripe (PayPal, Square, Authorize.net), live carrier shipping rates (USPS, FedEx), social sign-in (Google, Facebook, Apple) and the TitanCart extensions catalog are features of TitanCart Pro, are not present in this plugin’s code, and are documented in the Pro edition’s own materials.
